details: Bitcoin prices have been fluctuating around $64,000, touching a 24-hour low of $63,700. This movement follows a significant $225.18 million in net outflows from spot Bitcoin Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) on July 24th, with BlackRock's IBIT accounting for a substantial portion, effectively ending a seven-session inflow streak. The broader crypto market experienced a 1.1% decline in total capitalization, and the Crypto Fear & Greed Index remains in "fear" territory at 27, reflecting cautious investor sentiment. Ethereum also saw declines, and crypto derivatives trading volume dropped by 12.92%, further indicating reduced risk appetite.
title: Bitcoin Flirts with $64K as ETF Outflows Hit $225M, Market Sentiment "Fear"

details: In separate incidents, two Ethereum bridges have been exploited, resulting in a combined loss of $31.7 million within hours. Following these security breaches, a third protocol has taken the precautionary measure of halting its staking operations, highlighting ongoing vulnerabilities within the decentralized finance (DeFi) ecosystem and raising concerns about infrastructure security.
title: Two Ethereum Bridges Lose $31.7M in Exploits, Third Protocol Halts Staking

details: Ripple is expanding its efforts in the stablecoin sector by investing in Notabene to enhance RLUSD stablecoin payments for financial institutions. Additionally, Ripple has launched "Ripple Mint" to further broaden institutional access to its RLUSD stablecoin, signaling a strategic move to integrate the digital asset more deeply into traditional finance.
title: Ripple Doubles Down on RLUSD Stablecoin with Notabene Investment & Mint Launch

details: The World Foundation has successfully completed a strategic token sale, raising $52.5 million. The funding round was led by prominent blockchain investment firm Pantera Capital, with the capital earmarked to support the expansion of the World ID network and its underlying infrastructure.
title: World Foundation Secures $52.5M in Token Sale Led by Pantera Capital

details: Bitcoin mining company Poolin has filed for bankruptcy, reportedly owing 11,700 users a total of $164 million. This development signals significant financial distress within the mining sector and could have implications for those affected users and the broader crypto mining industry.
title: Bitcoin Mining Giant Poolin Files for Bankruptcy Amid $164M Debt
